scope: Theorem 2.1 (Classical Artin and Coxeter inputs) of the manuscript “Parabolic intersections in Artin groups” (preprints/Parabolic-intersections-in-Artin-groups-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 254 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4cd7fa316371447c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The group defined by the Artin presentation on T ⊆ S embeds in A, with image AT . No sphericity hypothesis is needed here. For a spherical T, the positive Artin monoid A+ T embeds in AT , is cancellative, and has greatest common divisors on both sides. Every element of AT is both a left fraction and a right fraction of positive elements. Any two elements a, b ∈ AT thus have a common positive extension pa = qb, with p, q ∈ A+ T . Reduced expressions in any Coxeter system are related by braid moves. They therefore define a positive lift ι(w) of a Coxeter element w. If T is spherical and wT is its longest element, the left and right divisors of ∆T = ι(wT ) are precisely {ι(w) : w ∈ WT }. In the finite geometric representation, root signs detect descents, the group acts simply transitively on chambers, and the translates of a closed fundamental chamber cover the entire dual space.
